summary: Re-test of Purchase History feature after sold_count=None fix. 18/18 tests passed (was 17/18 with 1 skipped). The $inc fix resolved the code path, but 106 existing contacts in the DB already had sold_count=None from the old bug — these were data-migrated to sold_count=0 to restore GET /api/contacts 200 responses.

critical.issue: Still returned 500 after the $inc fix because 106 existing DB documents had sold_count=null (written by the old buggy code). Pydantic model has sold_count: int = 0 (not Optional), so any null value causes ValidationError. Fixed by running a one-time DB migration: update_many({sold_count: None}, {$set: {sold_count: 0}}) — 106 docs updated.

action_items: IMPORTANT (preventive): The Contact Pydantic model has sold_count: int = 0 (not Optional[int]). Any future code that sets sold_count to None/null will break GET /api/contacts. Consider adding a DB-level validator or changing model to Optional[int] = 0 for safety.
Consider adding a startup migration in server.py to auto-heal sold_count=null contacts, in case this happens again.
critical_code_review_comments: models.py Contact: sold_count: int = 0 is strict — any null in DB breaks serialization. Recommend Optional[int] = 0 with a validator to coerce None→0 for resilience.
seed_data_creation: Test purchases created for contact with phone +15550000001 under user 69a0b7095fddcede09591667. DB migration: 106 contacts updated sold_count null→0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 18 purchase history tests now pass. The sold_count null issue in DB was fixed by data migration. The code fix ($inc) is in place. Legacy migration test now passes (found contacts with vehicle field). Broadcast filters all working.
rca_of_issue: Root cause: old add_purchase() used '$set: {sold_count: None}' which wrote null to MongoDB. Contact Pydantic model requires int. Fix: code changed to $inc but 106 docs already had null. Data migration required in addition to code fix.
